issues.area: events / concurrency: L5-R3 and L5-R13 invariants, R-SYN-12 (MUST, terminal events never dropped). Same class as L5-C1-00, found new this cycle.
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/EventForwarder.swift:309-314 (a retired engine's clientShutDown is dropped and its stream drained), together with Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/SubscriberQueue.swift:14, :47-48 and :108-114 (clientStarted and clientShutDown share the terminal .client slot; the newer one replaces the older and moves to the tail). The model's exemption that hides it: Tests/ZTronAssetKitTests/EventContinuityModelTests.swift:1234-1246.
issues.problem:
A consumer loses an intermediate generation's clientStarted.

Mechanism:
- The hand-over gives a follower a stream of generation g before g is installed.
- If the forwarder's pump has not read that stream when a second reopen retires g, g's shutdown publishes clientShutDown into the same .client slot of the unread queue, replacing clientStarted(g).
- The forwarder then hides that retired clientShutDown (G-2).
- So the consumer gets no event of that slot for g. It reads g's events, whose snapshot generation restarted (B-17), with no reset announced.

This contradicts L5-R3 ('The only exception is the engine's documented coalescing of non-terminal progress'). It also contradicts L5-R13 ('every event of each later generation from that generation's first event on (clientStarted included), subject only to the engine's documented coalescing of progress'). The .client slot is terminal (isProgress == false). G-16's wording ('per subject, H-9; a retired engine's clientShutDown is hidden') narrows the ruling, and no ruling authorises that.

PROVEN, 3 of 3 runs each:
- PROBE-C2-9: a subscribe() stream, not read across two reopens. An oracle subscribed to generation 1 at replacementBuilt shows what generation 1 published: [clientStarted(generation: 1), snapshotChanged(1), snapshotChanged(3), assetAvailable(x1, 3), clientShutDown]. The consumer received [snapshotChanged(2) (gen 0), snapshotChanged(3), assetAvailable(x1, 3), clientStarted(generation: 1) (gen 2's), snapshotChanged(3), assetAvailable(x2, 3)], so generation 1's clientStarted is missing. The control, which reads up to x1 before the second reopen, does receive it.
- PROBE-C2-17: an events stream that IS read, one event behind. Its first pull returned, then two generation-0 markers keep the pump in offer. Generation 1 published [clientStarted(1), assetAvailable(x1, 3), clientShutDown]. The consumer received [w0, w1, assetAvailable(x1, 3), clientStarted(1) (gen 2's), x2].

Why the model passes: I1 requires a generation's clientStarted only when the consumer received one of that generation's markers before its shutdown began. With that exemption removed for retired generations only (kept for the final generation, whose clientStarted the forwarded real clientShutDown may legitimately supersede), the model failed all 10 of 10 cases, at first seeds 1, 4, 5, 9, 32, 67, 70, 96, 108 and 183. Examples:
- 'seed 4: consumer 0 (subscribe(), registered at 3, live) lost clientStarted(generation: 1) of generation 1 (retired)'
- 'seed 5: consumer 0 (events, registered at 4, live) lost clientStarted(generation: 1) of generation 2 (retired)'
issues.fix:
Make a retired generation's clientStarted survive its own hidden clientShutDown.

(a) Recommended. This needs an orchestrator-authorised WP-F edit:
- In SubscriberQueue.swift's EventSlot, give clientShutDown its own terminal slot (for example .clientEnd), so it never replaces an undelivered clientStarted. The bound grows by one slot.
- I validated this in a scratch copy (.build-verify-g-c2-correct/probe2/pkg). PROBE-C2-9, PROBE-C2-17 and the model with the strict I1 (500 seeds) all pass, and all 78 Kit tests pass.
- Only two WP-F tests fail, because they pin the old mapping and need updating: EngineUnitTests.swift:145-161 'every event maps to the slot it coalesces under', and EngineEventsTests.swift:60 'slots.last == .client'. The H-9 bound text needs the same update.

(b) WP-G-only alternative:
- When the pump switches to a handed stream whose first event is not clientStarted, forward clientStarted(generation:) before that event.
- Build it from that engine's OpenReport.generation, which start() returns; performReopen and the callers' starts can record it.

In both cases:
- Tighten the model's I1 at EventContinuityModelTests.swift:1243-1246, so that every retired generation built after the registration owes its clientStarted. It must fail before the fix.
- Add PROBE-C2-9's and PROBE-C2-17's shapes to FacadeReopenTests as regression tests.
- Update G-2, G-16 and the EventForwarder doc comment.

(c) If the orchestrator instead accepts G-16's narrower promise, it should rule so explicitly. G-2, G-16 and §8 must then state the loss, and the item becomes non-blocking.

issues.area: reopen trigger after a replaced root (B-15 detection; a limit of L5-R4); outside WP-G (WP-B)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetStore+Commit.swift:158-159 (unavailable = .rootVanished is set only when a commit's verifyRoot fails); Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/AssetClient.swift:124-135 (the facade reopens only on the store's own flag)
issues.problem:
A replaced root that the store has not detected yet, because no commit happened since, is never reopened through sync or resolve. PROVEN by PROBE-C2-14 and PROBE-C2-15, 1 run each:
- sync(.force) returns failed(.storageUnavailable(.ioFailure)) from the staging listing.
- resolve fails with .serverUnavailable(retryAfter: nil) after 2 transfer attempts (staging fails with ENOENT).
- unavailableReason stays nil afterwards, so L5-R4's path (b) returns both failures as given, and the client stays on the dead root.

Detection waits for some later commit, for example reportUnreadable or a purge that deletes something. The tests always force detection first (markSyncDue in FacadeReopenTests.vanished). The facade follows the ruled behaviour, so this is not WP-G's defect.
issues.fix: Route to WP-B, or rule on it. The store's staging listing and its staging sink could run StoreLock.verifyRoot on ENOENT and set unavailable = .rootVanished; L5-R4's path (b) then reopens. Otherwise, record the limit under 'Not verified' next to the device rootVanished item.

issues.area: engine claims (L5-R15), a latent design fragility; unproven and unreachable today
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineCommands.swift:464-467 (a give-up's leftover claims are parked under releasing[token] for a group that is still registered) and Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineDispatch.swift:270-272 (isReleasedOnly treats every token in releasing as released)
issues.problem:
releasing[token] now also means 'claims left to drop' for a group that is still registered. If a join ever gave up with more than releasesPerTurn claims left after it had joined some members, those members' jobs (wanted by a live group) would count as released-only. They would be set aside and kept from dispatch until the follow-up drained the leftovers.

G-13 records that no running engine reaches such a give-up: state.remote is set once at start, and shutdown clears the groups first. I found no path that does. Not proven.
issues.fix: Optional: keep give-up leftovers in a table of their own, drained by the same follow-up. Alternatively, have isReleasedOnly and setsAside ignore tokens that are still in state.groups. That keeps the gate's meaning if the invariant ever breaks.

issues.area: tests / assertion strength (L5-R14's rework of R-STO-9)
issues.problem: The wait for the replacement's syncFinished matches by equality with the outcome sync() returned. In PROBE-C2-6, generation 0's launch syncFinished had the same runID (run-1), trigger (.launch), plan and counts as the replacement's run. Only finishedAt differed (22:13:20 against 22:13:21 on the fake clock). If the clock had not moved between the two runs, the wait would match generation 0's event, and the assertion would pass without the replacement's event. It is deterministic today, but it rests on a timestamp.
issues.fix: Require the matching syncFinished after the vanished root's failed(.storageUnavailable(.ioFailure)) event in the probe's received order. Alternatively, compare positions rather than values alone.

issues.area: tests / test strength: L5-R13 path 5 (a registration that a retired engine answered with .shutDown) is not pinned, and the model's I1 does not check it
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetKitTests/EventContinuityModelTests.swift:1196-1201 (per-generation I1 runs only for generations whose reopen began after the consumer's registeredAt), :827-830 with :1020-1023 (a subscribe() started while a reopen is parked before its install is stamped only when it settles) and :847-853 with :1031-1037 (an events stream is stamped at its first received event); Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/ClientLifecycle.swift:331-341 (path 5)
issues.problem: I wrote mutant MP5, which restores path 5's old shape: in register(_:)'s `.failure(.shutDown) where hasRetired` branch, after the reopen it does `self.unfollow(key); return await self.register(forwarder)`. That repeats the registration on the replacement and drops what the hand-over gave the follower. MP5 survives all 78 ZTronAssetKitTests in 3 of 3 runs, the 500-seed model included. MP5 is not an equivalent mutant. My scratch probe PROBE-P5 makes the first pull of an `events` stream while a reopen is parked at `replacementBuilt`, releases the reopen, waits until the pump holds an event of the replacement, then runs a maintenance marker. On HEAD the stream receives `clientStarted(generation: 1)` in 5 of 5 runs. Under MP5 it fails 3 of 3: the stream starts at the repeated registration's replay `[snapshotChanged(generation: 1), syncStarted(run-1, launch), syncFinished(run-1, .failed(.cancelled)), …]`, with no clientStarted. G-16 (g.md:126) promises such a stream every event of each later generation from its first event on, clientStarted included. L5-R13 lists path 5 as part of the class and asks the model's I1 to check what the promise says. The model never checks this case: it stamps the registration only after the parked reopen settled, and checks only generations built by reopens that began after that stamp. HEAD's code is correct here; no test would catch a regression.
issues.fix: Add PROBE-P5's shape as a deterministic regression test in FacadeRaceTests or FacadeReopenTests. It parks at `replacementBuilt` through SeamHold, makes the first pull of an `events` stream, or calls `subscribe()`, while parked, then opens the hold and asserts that the replacement's `clientStarted` and a later marker arrive. MP5 must fail it. Optionally strengthen the model too: for consumers that begin while parked before install, stamp registeredAt at the call's start (the follow turn), and run checkGeneration for every generation installed after that turn. Record the mutant in g.md.

issues.area: tests / L5-R14 completeness: pattern (e) in a cycle-2 test that the enumeration lists as clean
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetKitTests/FacadeRaceTests.swift:324-370 (eventsStreamCancelledDuringItsRegistration; cancel at :358, hold.open() at :359, assertion at :363); Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/EventForwarder.swift:164-169 (cancel() spawns stop() in an unordered Task); docs/adr-drafts/g.md:237 ("FacadeRaceTests (all 8: seam holds and condition waits …)")
issues.problem: `#expect(received == 0)` asserts an exact count of the events a cancelled consumer happened to pull (L5-R14 pattern (e)). It holds only if the forwarder's asynchronous `stop()` hop, which `cancel()` spawns, reaches the actor before the registration returns. The test opens the hold immediately after `consumer.cancel()`, and nothing orders the two. In the other order, `next()` starts the pump on the stream it was handed. The pump hands the replacement's first event to the in-flight pull, which `AsyncStream(unfolding:)` still returns after cancellation, so `received` becomes 1. The exit the g.md says this test covers (EventForwarder.swift:147-151) is then skipped. A scratch probe that only delays `stop()` until after the reopen fails the test 3 of 3 with "the cancelled consumer received nothing: 1". On unmodified code FacadeRaceTests passed 100 of 100 at 1-minute load 17.8–233, so I did not observe a flake.
issues.fix: Order the two steps explicitly. Add a test-only hook on EventForwarder, `nil` in production like `offerParked`, called at the end of `stop()`, and await it before `hold.open()`. Then `received == 0` and the :147-151 exit hold in every schedule. Add the row (FacadeRaceTests.eventsStreamCancelledDuringItsRegistration → (e) → conversion) to the L5-R14 table.

issues.area: rulings / records consistency for ADR-054 (L5-R13 promise wording)
issues.location: docs/adr-drafts/g.md:126 (G-16 "subject only to the engine's coalescing (one slot per progress key and per subject, H-9 …)") vs .build-orchestrator/l5-rulings.md:164 ("subject only to the engine's documented coalescing of progress")
issues.problem: G-16 and the model (EventContinuityModelTests I1: a generation's clientStarted is required only once one of its markers arrived) allow the engine's per-subject coalescing (ARCHITECTURE §7.9, "terminal events coalesce per subject"). As a result, a retired generation's unread `clientStarted` is superseded by that generation's `clientShutDown`, and the forwarder then hides it (G-2). The ruling's promise excepts only the coalescing of progress. The behaviour is the engine's documented behaviour and is consistent with G-2, but the recorded promise is wider than the ruling's text.
issues.fix: The orchestrator confirms in ADR-054 that the exception is the engine's documented coalescing per progress key and per subject, as G-16 states. Otherwise it rules that a retired generation's superseded `clientStarted` must still reach the stream. No code change if confirmed.

FAIL: 1 blocking issue, which I found new in this cycle. It belongs to L5-R13's class (lost events across reopens). Every finding that blocked in cycle 1 is fixed, and I reproduced each fix with my own probes against the new code.

- **L5-C1-00/03 fixed.** An unpulled subscribe() stream now follows reopens. PROBE-C2-1 holds one unpulled stream across two reopens and gets both generations' markers in order, plus the final replacement's clientStarted. PROBE-C2-7 serves a call while the reopen is parked after the install, and the unpulled stream gets the replacement's clientStarted and the call's event. PROBE-C2-8 drops an unpulled stream during a parked reopen and leaves nothing behind. Each ran 3 of 3.
- **L5-C1-04 fixed.** PROBE-C2-2 and -3 make an events stream's first pull while a reopen is parked at replacementBuilt and before the old engine's shutdown. The follower is recorded during the park, and the reader gets clientStarted, then the marker.
- **L5-C1-01 fixed.** PROBE-C2-6 shows generation 0 now downloads the asset in every run (1 start before the baseline). The baseline count gives exactly 1 for the replacement; the old whole-log count would give 2 every time.
- **L5-C1-02 fixed.** The R-CAR-3 pair passed 50 of 50, at loads up to 11.98.

I also checked L5-R13's other invariants:
- PROBE-C2-16 puts a shutdown inside the hand-over loop (17, 6 and 6 of 60 streams handed). Nothing is installed, every stream ends with exactly one clientShutDown, and no follower or subscriber is left.
- PROBE-C2-4 and -5 shut down while a reopen is parked, with the same clean result.
- The model passed 3,000 seeds.
- I reviewed the cycle-2 forwarder and lifecycle code: register(_:), the same-turn hand-over and install, held/takeHandover, stop() and end(), and the removed startPump guard. I found no reentrancy, double-resume, leak or ordering defect. Every new await has a REENTRANCY row (g-7, g-9, g-10, g-11).
- The L5-R15 engine edits (chunked endClaims, the merge in performReleaseGroup, shutdown clearing the parked claims) are sound. Sync under TSan passed 321 tests with 0 reports.
- L5-R2's spawn table is complete: 23 sites, and every line number matches HEAD.
- No new API needs a check against the iOS 15 floor, and the generic iOS build is clean.

**The blocking defect.** A consumer can lose an intermediate generation's clientStarted. This happens when its pump has not yet read the stream the hand-over gave it for that generation, and a second reopen retires that generation. The engine queue keeps clientStarted and clientShutDown in one terminal slot, so the retirement's clientShutDown replaces the unread clientStarted. The forwarder then hides that retired clientShutDown, so the consumer gets no event of that slot at all. It is deterministic (3 of 3) for an unpulled subscribe() stream (PROBE-C2-9) and for an events stream that is one event behind (PROBE-C2-17). This contradicts L5-R3 ("The only exception is the engine's documented coalescing of non-terminal progress") and L5-R13 ("clientStarted included … coalescing of progress").

The model misses it because of an exemption in its I1 check. With that exemption removed for retired generations only, the model fails in all 10 of 10 cases.

**Other runs.** Every gate and run I made passed. I left the worktree unmodified: git status is clean at 9619770. I did not run --gates-only or --full, so TRACEABILITY.md was untouched.
